column1: # Hand-checked readings that win over every other source.
# One per line: term<TAB>reading (lower-case, tone marks, one syllable per Han character, separated by spaces).
# A line applies to the headword it names and, when the term is two or more Han characters, to every
# longer headword that contains it (重吸收 also fixes 肾小管重吸收作用). A one-character line is weaker:
# it is the reading of that character wherever no word covers it, i.e. it replaces pypinyin's default.
# Add a term here when CC-CEDICT does not list it, or lists a reading that is wrong in medicine, and the
# result is misread. `python -m medical_yomitan golden` keeps the important ones checked.
# -- Characters whose usual reading in medical terms is not pypinyin's default
# -- Other words pypinyin or a wrong word boundary misreads
# -- CC-CEDICT lists two readings and the everyday one is not the medical one
# -- CC-CEDICT words that are right in everyday speech and wrong inside a medical term: a neutral tone
#    (包涵 bāo han, 太阳 tài yang, 栓子 shuān zi), or a word across a boundary (性子 in 功能失调性子宫出血,
#    生分 in 叉生分析). An override is placed before CC-CEDICT's words, so 子宫 here keeps 性子 out.
# -- 塞: sài in transliterated names (the one-character line above), but
# -- 相 xiàng (phase) where pypinyin sees 相对 or reads xiāng
# -- 散 sǎn (a powder) at the end of a preparation's name
